user.title: Smart Shutter Control
user.description: The base controller holds the settings for all shutters. Add the shutters afterwards on the integration page.

data_description.wind_gust: Optional; the storm limit applies to the wind speed and the gusts.
data_description.sun_source: Is it sunny? From PV power or from light sensors, never both. None: the weather entity, else the sun's position only.

data_description.wind_gust: Optional; the storm limit applies to the wind speed and the gusts.
data_description.sun_source: Is it sunny? From PV power or from light sensors, never both. None: the weather entity, else the sun's position only.

pv.title: PV power
pv.description: The PV power tells how much the sun shines: the integration learns the clear-sky power for each position of the sun.

data_description.pv_power: One or more sensors; they are added up. Used as a measure of clouds.
data_description.pv_peak: Peak power of the panels, for the expected power in clear sky.

light.title: Light sensors
light.description:
The highest light sensor counts. The integration learns the clear-sky value for each position of the sun; until then it is sunny from the limit below.

Highest in the last 30 days:
{maxima}

Direct sun gives 50 000–100 000 lx. A sensor that never comes above about 10 000 lx probably saturates and cannot tell sun from bright cloud.

data_description.light_sensors: Sensors with device class illuminance; the highest value counts.
data_description.lux_limit: Used during the first days, until the integration has learned the clear-sky value.

error.saturates: A sensor stays below 10 000 lx in the last 30 days and probably saturates. Choose another sensor, or submit again to use it anyway.

storm.title: Storm and frost
storm.description: In a storm shutters with automatic control are only fully open or fully closed; during frost they do not move.

data_description.storm_wind_limit: Highest in the last 30 days: {wind_max} km/h. Empty: not used.
data_description.storm_gust_limit: Highest in the last 30 days: {gust_max} km/h. Empty: not used.
data_description.storm_release: Minutes after the last value above a limit.
data_description.frost_limit: During frost the shutters do not move automatically (they may be frozen).

data_description.sunny_threshold: PV power or light (lux) as a share of its clear-sky value at this position of the sun. With light sensors, the fixed lux limit applies until the clear-sky value is learned.
data_description.max_incidence: Sun at a larger angle to the window counts as not shining on it.
data_description.heat_room: Only for shutters with a room temperature sensor.
data_description.close_delay: Minutes of sun on the window before the shutter goes down.
data_description.open_delay: Minutes without sun before it goes up again.

schedule.title: Base schedule
schedule.description: The schedule every shutter follows, unless it overrides a setting on its own schedule page.

data.winter_closed_below: Winter: closed all day at or below

data_description.slit_module: Only used when the shutter is not calibrated; with a calibration the slit is the measured lift point.
data_description.winter_closed_below: Empty: off. A manual action overrides it.

holidays.title: Holidays
holidays.description: On weekend days and holidays the schedules use their weekend times. Choose the calendar with the holidays; its holidays are shown on the next page.

data_description.holiday_calendar: A calendar of Home Assistant's Holiday integration (Settings → Devices & services → Add integration → Holiday).

holiday_days.title: Holidays of the calendar

data_description.holidays_disabled: Checked holidays count as normal days, every year. The list shows the holidays of the chosen calendar (after saving it once).

data_description.holidays_excluded: Dates from the calendar that count as normal days, same format.

winter.title: Winter
winter.description: Winter mode is on while the mean outdoor temperature of the last 24 hours is below the limit (with the select Winter mode on auto).

language.title: Language
language.description: Language of the card and the entity names. Settings screens and state values in Home Assistant's own cards follow your profile language.

error.bad_dates: Lines {lines} could not be read: use 2026-12-24 or 12-31.

horizon.title: Horizon
horizon.description: Set the lowest sun elevation for each sun direction. Values are interpolated between points. Press “Sun has left the window” when the sun disappears behind an obstruction to record a point.

data_description.rows: Add, change or remove rows. Leave the table empty for no horizon profile.

add_point.title: Add a calibration point
add_point.description: The shutter first moves to closed (↑) or open (↓), then to the module position, and asks for the opening.

cal_measure.title: Measure
cal_measure.description: The shutter is at module position {position} % ({direction}) {reached}. How far is the window open below the bottom bar ({unit})? 0 if the bar is still on the sill.

cal_lift.title: Bottom bar
cal_lift.description: Module position {position} % from closed. Has the bottom bar left the sill?

cal_review.title: Result

schedule.title: Schedule overrides
schedule.description: Leave a field empty (or 'Inherit') to follow the base schedule; the base value is shown under each field.

data.winter_closed_below: Winter: closed all day at or below

calibrate.title: Calibrate
calibrate.description: Let the assistant move the shutter and ask for measurements, or edit the measured points yourself.

cal_assistant.title: Calibrate
cal_assistant.description:
First the assistant looks for the point where the bottom bar leaves the sill: from closed it moves up in small steps and asks whether the bar has lifted. Then it measures four points spread over the travel above that point, from closed and from open, and asks each time how far the window is open below the bottom bar. Automatic control of this shutter is paused meanwhile.

Enter the window height to measure in cm, or leave it empty to estimate in % of the window.

cal_table.title: Calibration table
cal_table.description: A row per module position (the position the module reports, %), with the measured opening below the bottom bar in % of the window: going up (the shutter came from below) and going down (it came from above). A cell may stay empty. At least two points in one direction are needed; a direction with fewer uses the other one.

data_description.slit_up: Module position with the slat gaps open and the bottom bar still on the sill. Optional.
data_description.slit_down: Module position with the slat gaps open and the bottom bar still on the sill. Optional.

cal_table_review.title: Result
